title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description:
Serialization is the process of converting a data structure or object into a sequence of bits or a string so that it can be stored in a file or memory buffer, or transmitted across a network connection link to be reconstructed later in the same or another computer environment.

Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree. There is no restriction on how your serialization/deserialization algorithm should work. You just need to ensure that a binary tree can be serialized to a string and this string can be deserialized to an **identical** new binary tree structure.

Implement the `Codec` class:
- `serialize(root)` encodes a tree into a single string without modifying the input tree.
- `deserialize(data)` decodes your encoded string into a newly constructed binary tree.

The judge invokes `serialize` and `deserialize` on separate `Codec` instances and verifies that the reconstructed tree matches the original tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: A single traversal order (such as level-order BFS or preorder DFS) uniquely determines a binary tree as long as you explicitly record null children with a sentinel token (e.g., `#`).
Use a delimiter (such as a comma `,`) between tokens so multi-digit numbers and negative values are parsed unambiguously.
With level-order BFS, push children (or `#`) into a queue during `serialize`, and during `deserialize` pop parents from a queue while reading two tokens at a time for their left and right children.

examples.explanation: Serializing [1,2,3,null,null,4,5] to a string and deserializing it reconstructs the exact same tree.
An empty tree serializes and deserializes back to an empty tree.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Level-order array representation of the binary tree
